chapters.title: The LORD Is a Jealous and Avenging God
chapters.html:
Nahum 1

The LORD Takes Vengeance

1The oracle concerning Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.

2The LORD is a jealous and avenging God;
the LORD is avenging and full of wrath;
the LORD takes vengeance on His adversaries
and keeps His wrath for His enemies.

3The LORD is slow to anger and great in power,
and not leaving it unpunished.
His way is in the whirlwind and in the storm,
and the clouds are the dust of His feet.

4He rebukes the sea and dries it up,
and makes all the rivers run dry;
Bashan and Carmel waste away,
and the flower of Lebanon wastes away.

5The mountains quake before Him,
and the hills melt;
the earth heaves at His presence,
the world and those who live in it.

6Who can stand before His indignation?
Who can rise up against His burning anger?
His wrath is poured out like fire,
and the rocks are broken apart by Him.

7The LORD is good,
a stronghold on the day of distress;
He knows those who take refuge in Him.

8But with an overflowing flood passing through
He will make a full end of her place,
and He will pursue His enemies into darkness.

Distress Will Not Rise Twice

9What do you devise against the LORD?
He will make a full end;
distress will not rise up twice.

10For though they are like tangled thorns,
and drunk as with their drink,
they will be consumed like stubble, fully dried.

11From you has come out one who devises evil against the LORD,
a worthless counselor.

12This is what the LORD says:
Though they are at full strength and many,
even so they will be sheared off and pass away.
Though I have afflicted you,
I will afflict you no more.

13So now I will break his yoke bar from off you
and tear off your bonds.

14The LORD has commanded concerning you:
No more descendants will bear your name.
From the house of your gods I will cut off
the carved image and the cast image.
I will make your grave,
for you are of no account.

15There on the mountains, the feet of one who brings good news,
who proclaims peace!
Keep your feasts, Judah;
pay your vows;
for the worthless one will no longer pass through you;
he is cut off completely.

Notes

  • v1 "The oracle concerning Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum" — massa, oracle, as in The oracle concerning Tyre (Isaiah 23:1). Sefer chazon, the book of the vision, is found only here: no other prophet's heading calls itself a book. Nachum, Nahum, is the root of nacham, comfort, as in Comfort, comfort My people (Isaiah 40:1). Elkoshite names a town not mentioned elsewhere. In the Hebrew text v15 is 2:1; the English numbering is followed, and the Greek follows it too. The city is the Nineveh that turned and was spared in Jonah (Jonah 3:10; 4:11).

  • v2 "a jealous and avenging God… takes vengeance… keeps His wrath for His enemies" — El qanno, a jealous God, is Joshua's word, He is a jealous God (Joshua 24:19), and noqem, avenging, is said three times. Noqem… ve-noter are the two verbs the law forbids to an Israelite, You shall not take revenge and you shall not hold a grudge against the sons of your people (Leviticus 19:18); here they belong to the LORD, against His enemies. The psalm says of His people, nor will He keep His anger forever (Psalm 103:9), with the same verb. Ba'al chemah, word for word master of wrath, is full of wrath.

  • vv2–8 the order of the lines — the poem begins its lines, with gaps, with the letters of the alphabet in order: El (aleph, v2), be-sufah (bet, v3), go'er (gimel, v4), harim (he, v5), va-tissa (vav, v5), chamato (chet, v6), tov (tet, v7), and kalah (kaf) inside v8. Some letters are missing or out of place, and the pattern is not carried past v8.

  • v3 "The LORD is slow to anger and great in power, and not leaving it unpunished" — the LORD's name from Sinai, as Moses gave it back in his prayer, The LORD is slow to anger and abundant in loyal love… and not leaving it unpunished (Numbers 14:18), with great in power where Moses had abundant in loyal love. Ve-naqqeh lo yenaqqeh is the doubled verb of and not leaving it unpunished (Exodus 34:7). Jonah gave the mercy of the name as his reason for fleeing (Jonah 4:2); Nahum gives the other half. Sufah, whirlwind, as in they will reap the whirlwind (Hosea 8:7), and se'arah, storm, the storm out of which the LORD answered Job (Job 38:1).

  • vv4–6 "He rebukes the sea and dries it up… Who can stand before His indignation?" — the sea of the exodus, He rebuked the Sea of Reeds, and it dried up (Psalm 106:9), and Isaiah's By My rebuke I dry up the sea (Isaiah 50:2). Bashan, Carmel and Lebanon umlal, waste away, as in Hosea 4:3. The hills melt is Amos 9:13, and the world and those who live in it is The earth is the LORD's… the world and those who live in it (Psalm 24:1). Mi ya'amod, who can stand, as in who can stand before You once Your anger is roused? (Psalm 76:7); nittekhah, is poured out, as in My anger and My wrath will be poured out (Jeremiah 7:20).

  • vv7–8 "a stronghold on the day of distress… with an overflowing flood passing through" — ma'oz, stronghold, as in Joel 3:16, and chosei vo, those who take refuge in Him, as in Blessed are all who take refuge in him (Psalm 2:12). The flood is Isaiah's picture of Assyria itself, it will sweep on into Judah, overflowing and passing through (Isaiah 8:8), turned against Nineveh. Kalah, a full end, is what the LORD would not make of Judah, yet I will not make a full end (Jeremiah 4:27). Meqomah, her place, is Nineveh's. Ve-oyevav yeraddef choshekh is He will pursue His enemies into darkness, or darkness will pursue His enemies, as the Greek has it.

  • vv9–11 "What do you devise against the LORD?… tangled thorns… a worthless counselor" — chashav, devise, the verb of Micah 2:1, now said of Nineveh; yo'ets beliyya'al, a worthless counselor, as the law's worthless men (Deuteronomy 13:13). Lo taqum pa'amayim tsarah, distress will not rise up twice: the LORD will not need a second blow. v10 is obscure: ad sirim sevukhim u-khe-sov'am sevu'im, a run of like sounds, tangled thorns and drunk… drunk; its sense is uncertain, and the Greek has for to its foundation it will be laid bare, and like twisted bindweed it will be devoured.

  • vv12–14 "they will be sheared off… I will break his yoke bar… you are of no account" — nagozzu, sheared off, is the shearing of sheep, Laban had gone to shear his flock (Genesis 31:19). The you changes: I have afflicted you is Judah, as is your bonds, from the promise I will break his yoke from off your neck and tear off your bonds (Jeremiah 30:8); the yoke bar is the LORD's own word in the law, I broke the bars of your yoke (Leviticus 26:13). In v14 you is masculine, Nineveh's king: the carved image and the cast image of the law's curse (Deuteronomy 27:15). Qalota, you are of no account, word for word you are light, as in those who despise Me shall be lightly esteemed (1 Samuel 2:30).

  • v15 "the feet of one who brings good news, who proclaims peace!… the worthless one will no longer pass through you" — Isaiah has the same words, How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of him who brings good news, who proclaims peace (Isaiah 52:7). The good news here is that Nineveh has fallen. Chaggi… chaggayikh, word for word feast your feasts, is keep your feasts, and pay your vows is Jonah's what I have vowed I will pay (Jonah 2:9). Beliyya'al, the worthless one, is the counselor of v11, and will no longer pass through you is Joel's word for strangers (Joel 3:17).

chapters.title: Where Is the Lions' Den?
chapters.html:
Nahum 2

The Attack on Nineveh

1The scatterer has come up against you.
Guard the rampart!
Watch the road!
Brace your loins!
Gather all your strength!

2For the LORD is restoring the pride of Jacob,
like the pride of Israel,
for plunderers have emptied them
and ruined their vine branches.

3The shield of his warriors is red;
the men of valor are clothed in scarlet;
the chariots flash with steel
on the day he makes ready,
and the cypress spears are brandished.

4The chariots drive madly in the streets;
they rush to and fro in the squares;
their appearance is like torches;
they dart like lightning.

5He calls his nobles to mind;
they stumble as they go;
they hurry to her wall,
and the shelter is set up.

6The gates of the rivers are opened,
and the palace melts away.

7It is fixed: she is stripped, she is carried off,
and her slave women moan like the sound of doves,
beating on their breasts.

8Nineveh is like a pool of water,
all her days;
and they flee.
"Stand! Stand!"
But no one turns back.

9Plunder the silver!
Plunder the gold!
There is no end to the treasure,
the weight of every precious thing.

10Empty, emptied, and laid waste!
Hearts melt and knees give way;
anguish is in all loins,
and all faces grow pale.

The Lions' Den

11Where is the lions' den,
the feeding place of the young lions,
where the lion and the lioness walked,
and the lion's cub,
with no one to make them afraid?

12The lion tore enough for his cubs
and strangled prey for his lionesses;
he filled his caves with prey
and his dens with torn flesh.

13I am against you, declares the LORD of hosts.
I will burn her chariots in smoke,
and the sword will devour your young lions;
I will cut off your prey from the earth,
and the voice of your messengers
will no longer be heard.

Notes

  • v1 "The scatterer has come up against you. Guard the rampart!" — in the Hebrew text vv1–13 are 2:2–14; the English numbering is followed. Mefits, the scatterer, is the one who breaks a people apart; a word with nearly the same letters, mappets, is the war club of Jeremiah 51:20, You are My war club, My weapon of war. Natsor metsurah, guard the rampart, and the commands that follow are said to Nineveh as the attack begins.

  • v2 "the LORD is restoring the pride of Jacob… for plunderers have emptied them" — ge'on Ya'aqov, the pride of Jacob, the words of the psalm, the pride of Jacob, whom He loves (Psalm 47:4); in Amos the LORD said of the same thing I abhor the pride of Jacob (Amos 6:8), and here He restores it. Boqeqim, plunderers, from baqaq, empty, as in The LORD is about to empty the earth and lay it waste (Isaiah 24:1); the same verb comes back in v10. Zemoreihem, their vine branches, as in the vine branch (Ezekiel 15:2).

  • vv3–4 "the shield of his warriors is red… the cypress spears are brandished… The chariots drive madly in the streets" — the attackers come on in red and scarlet; metulla'im, clothed in scarlet, from tola, the scarlet of red like crimson (Isaiah 1:18). Be-esh peladot, flash with steel, is uncertain: peladot is found only here. Ve-ha-beroshim, the cypresses, are the spear shafts; the Greek has the horsemen, parashim, nearly the same letters. Yit-holelu ha-rekhev, the chariots drive madly, are Jeremiah's words, Drive madly, you chariots! (Jeremiah 46:9), and yishtaqshequn, rush to and fro, is from shaqaq, the verb of the locusts that leap on the city (Joel 2:9).

  • vv5–6 "they hurry to her wall… The gates of the rivers are opened, and the palace melts away" — who calls his nobles to mind, the attacker or Nineveh's king, the line does not say. Ha-sokhekh, the shelter, is a covering, the verb of the cherubim sheltering the cover (Exodus 25:20). Sha'arei ha-neharot, the gates of the rivers: The water recalls the flood of 1:8. Namog, melts away, as in He who touches the earth and it melts (Amos 9:5).

  • v7 "It is fixed: she is stripped, she is carried off… beating on their breasts" — obscure. Ve-hutstsav, it is fixed, can also be read as a name; gulletah, she is stripped, is from galah, to uncover and to go into exile; ho'alatah, she is carried off, word for word she is brought up. The Greek has the foundation is uncovered, and she was going up. Metofefot, beating, is the verb of the tambourine, young women playing tambourines (Psalm 68:25): the slave women beat their breasts like drums. The doves are Ezekiel's, like doves of the valleys, all of them moaning (Ezekiel 7:16).

  • vv8–9 "Nineveh is like a pool of water… Stand! Stand! But no one turns back… There is no end to the treasure" — mimei hi, all her days, is obscure; the Greek has her waters. Imdu amodu, Stand! Stand!, the officers' cry to men already running. Ve-ein qetseh la-tekhunah, there is no end to the treasure, as Isaiah said of Judah's riches, there is no end to their treasures (Isaiah 2:7). Kavod, weight, is also the word for glory.

  • v10 "Empty, emptied, and laid waste!… all faces grow pale" — buqah u-mevuqah u-mevullaqah, three words of nearly one sound, the empty… lay waste of Isaiah 24:1. Lev names, hearts melt, as at Jericho, our hearts melted (Joshua 2:11); chalchalah, anguish, as in my loins are filled with anguish (Isaiah 21:3). Kol panim qibbetsu fa'rur, all faces grow pale, is the phrase of Joel 2:6, the only other place it is found, and the English is Joel's.

  • vv11–12 "Where is the lions' den… the lion and the lioness… the lion's cub, with no one to make them afraid?" — Assyria is the lion, in the very words of Jacob's blessing of Judah, A lion's cub is Judah… like a lion, and like a lioness (Genesis 49:9), gur aryeh, aryeh, lavi. Ve-ein macharid, with no one to make them afraid, is the peace promised Israel, no one shall make them afraid (Micah 4:4), which the lion of Nineveh kept for itself. Mechanneq, strangled, is the verb of Ahithophel, he hanged himself (2 Samuel 17:23), and terefah, torn flesh, the law's Flesh torn in the field you shall not eat (Exodus 22:31). The question Where? is asked of a den now empty.

  • v13 "I am against you… the voice of your messengers will no longer be heard" — hineni elayikh, I am against you, as the LORD says to Tyre (Ezekiel 26:3) and to Babylon (Jeremiah 50:31). Mal'akhekheh, your messengers, with an ending found only here. They are the messengers of the king of Assyria, to whom the LORD said through Isaiah, By your messengers you have defied the Lord (2 Kings 19:23); against them stands the one who brings good news (1:15).

chapters.title: Woe to the City of Bloodshed
chapters.html:
Nahum 3

The City of Bloodshed

1Woe to the city of bloodshed,
all of it full of lies and plunder;
the prey never leaves it!

2The sound of the whip,
the sound of the rumbling wheel,
the galloping horse,
the skipping chariot!

3The horseman charging,
the flame of the sword,
the lightning of the spear,
a multitude of the slain,
heaps of corpses,
no end to the bodies;
they stumble over their bodies —

4all because of the great prostitution of the prostitute,
graceful and fair, mistress of sorceries,
who sells nations by her prostitution
and clans by her sorceries.

5I am against you, declares the LORD of hosts;
I will lift up your skirts over your face,
and show the nations your nakedness
and the kingdoms your shame.

6I will throw loathsome things on you,
and treat you with contempt,
and make you a spectacle.

7And it shall come to pass that all who see you
will flee from you and say,
"Nineveh is laid waste;
who will mourn for her?"
Where shall I seek comforters for you?

Are You Better Than No-amon?

8Are you better than No-amon,
who sat by the streams of the Nile,
with water all around her,
whose rampart was the sea,
the sea her wall?

9Cush was her strength, and Egypt,
without end;
Put and the Libyans were your helpers.

10Yet she too went into exile,
into captivity;
her little ones too were dashed to pieces
at the head of every street;
they cast lots for her honored men,
and all her great men were bound in chains.

11You too will be drunk;
you will be hidden;
you too will seek a stronghold from the enemy.

12All your fortresses are fig trees
with first-ripe figs:
if they are shaken,
they fall into the mouth of the eater.

13Your troops are women among you;
the gates of your land are wide open to your enemies;
fire has devoured your bars.

Like the Locust

14Draw water for the siege;
strengthen your fortresses;
go into the clay and tread the mortar;
take hold of the brick kiln!

15There the fire will devour you;
the sword will cut you off;
it will devour you as the young locust devours.
Make yourself as heavy as the young locust;
make yourself as heavy as the locust!

16You multiplied your merchants
more than the stars of the heavens;
the young locust strips and flies away.

17Your guards are like the locust,
your marshals like a cloud of locusts
that settle in the walls on a cold day;
the sun rises and they flee,
and no one knows where they are.

18Your shepherds slumber, king of Assyria;
your nobles lie still;
your people are scattered on the mountains,
with no one to gather them.

19There is no easing your hurt;
your wound is grievous.
All who hear the news of you
clap their hands over you;
for on whom has your evil not passed continually?

Notes

  • vv1–3 "Woe to the city of bloodshed… no end to the bodies" — Hoy ir damim, nearly the words of Ezekiel's woe on Jerusalem, Woe to the city of bloodshed (Ezekiel 24:6), now said of Nineveh. Teref, prey, is the word of the lion's den (2:12–13). The battle comes in short cries without verbs, sound after sound. Ve-ein qetseh la-geviyyah, no end to the bodies, are the words of no end to the treasure (2:9), and without end comes again in v9. Sus doher, the galloping horse, as in the galloping, galloping of his stallions (Judges 5:22), and meraqqedah, skipping, as the chariots of Joel 2:5. Written yikkashelu, read ve-khashelu, they stumble: the same verb.

  • v4 "the great prostitution of the prostitute… mistress of sorceries" — zenunim and keshafim, prostitution and sorceries, the pair that Jehu threw in Joram's face, the whoring of your mother Jezebel and her many sorceries (2 Kings 9:22). The city is a prostitute who sells: what she trades is nations and clans. Zonah and zenunim are the plain words, as in a wife of prostitution (Hosea 1:2).

  • vv5–6 "I will lift up your skirts over your face… loathsome things" — the LORD's words to Jerusalem in Jeremiah, I Myself will lift up your skirts over your face, and your shame will be seen (Jeremiah 13:26), now turned on Nineveh. Ve-nibbaltikh, treat you with contempt, is the verb of son treats father with contempt (Micah 7:6). Ke-ro'i, a spectacle, from ra'ah, see: v7 goes on, all who see you.

  • v7 "who will mourn for her? Where shall I seek comforters for you?" — mi yanud lah, who will mourn for her, as in Who will mourn for you? (Jeremiah 15:5). Menachamim, comforters, is from nacham, the root of the prophet's own name (1:1): Nahum, comfort, finds no one to comfort Nineveh. The question is Isaiah's to Zion, by whom shall I comfort you? (Isaiah 51:19), and the cry of Lamentations, she has no one to comfort her (Lamentations 1:2).

  • vv8–10 "Are you better than No-amon… Cush… Put and the Libyans… her little ones too were dashed to pieces" — No Amon is the Egyptian city of Amon of No (Jeremiah 46:25), the No that Ezekiel saw broken open (Ezekiel 30:16). Ye'orim, the streams of the Nile, as in the streams of Egypt (Isaiah 19:6). Cush, Egypt and Put are sons of Ham in the table of nations (Genesis 10:6), and the Libyans marched with Shishak (2 Chronicles 12:3). Her fall reads as Samaria's: their little ones will be dashed to pieces (Hosea 13:16), at the head of every street (Lamentations 2:19), and the lots cast for captives as in Joel 3:3. Nikhbaddeiha… ziqqim, her honored men… chains, as in to bind their kings with chains and their honored men with fetters of iron (Psalm 149:8). The Greek reads v8 quite differently: Prepare a portion, tune the string.

  • vv11–13 "You too will be drunk… fig trees with first-ripe figs… Your troops are women among you" — tishkeri, you will be drunk, the drinking of the cup (Obadiah 16). Ma'oz, stronghold, is what the LORD is to those who take refuge in Him (1:7); Nineveh will look for one from the enemy. The figs are Isaiah's picture, a first-ripe fig before the summer: whoever sees it swallows it as soon as it is in his hand (Isaiah 28:4). Women… bars are the words Jeremiah gives the fall of Babylon, they have become like women; her dwellings are set on fire; her bars are broken (Jeremiah 51:30).

  • v14 "Draw water for the siege… go into the clay and tread the mortar; take hold of the brick kiln!" — a taunt: get ready for a siege. Mei matsor, water for the siege, the matsor of Micah 5:1. Chomer, mortar, and bricks were Israel's labor in Egypt, in mortar and in bricks (Exodus 1:14), and the mortar of Babel (Genesis 11:3); now Nineveh must tread it. Malben, brick kiln, as in 2 Samuel 12:31.

  • vv15–17 "Make yourself as heavy as the young locust… the locust… a cloud of locusts" — three locust words: yeleq, young locust, arbeh, locust, and gov govai, word for word locusts of locusts, the gov of Amos's vision, He was forming locusts (Amos 7:1). Hitkabbed, make yourself heavy, is the weight of the locusts of Egypt, very heavy (Exodus 10:14). You multiplied your merchants more than the stars uses the blessing of Abraham, I will multiply your seed as the stars of the heavens (Genesis 22:17), for a trader's crowd that, like locusts, strips and flies off. Tafsserayikh, your marshals, is the word of appoint a marshal against her (Jeremiah 51:27). Minnezarayikh, your guards, is found only here, and its sense is a guess.

  • vv18–19 "Your shepherds slumber… scattered on the mountains… on whom has your evil not passed continually?" — the rulers are shepherds, and the people are left as in Micaiah's vision, all Israel scattered on the mountains, like sheep that have no shepherd (1 Kings 22:17). Nachlah makkatekha, your wound is grievous, are the words of Your hurt is incurable, your wound is grievous (Jeremiah 30:12), said there of Zion and here of Nineveh. Taq'u khaf, clap their hands, is the clapping of Clap your hands, all you peoples (Psalm 47:1). The book ends, as Jonah does, on a question, and its last word but one is ra'atkha, your evil, the evil that has come up before Me (Jonah 1:2).

Yet she too went into exile, into captivity; her little ones too were dashed to pieces at the head of every street; they cast lots for her honored men, and all her great men were bound in chains.
You too will be drunk; you will be hidden; you too will seek a stronghold from the enemy.
All your fortresses are fig trees with first-ripe figs: if they are shaken, they fall into the mouth of the eater.
Your troops are women among you; the gates of your land are wide open to your enemies; fire has devoured your bars.
Like the Locust
Draw water for the siege; strengthen your fortresses; go into the clay and tread the mortar; take hold of the brick kiln!
There the fire will devour you; the sword will cut you off; it will devour you as the young locust devours. Make yourself as heavy as the young locust; make yourself as heavy as the locust!
You multiplied your merchants more than the stars of the heavens; the young locust strips and flies away.
Your guards are like the locust, your marshals like a cloud of locusts that settle in the walls on a cold day; the sun rises and they flee, and no one knows where they are.
Your shepherds slumber, king of Assyria; your nobles lie still; your people are scattered on the mountains, with no one to gather them.
There is no easing your hurt; your wound is grievous. All who hear the news of you clap their hands over you; for on whom has your evil not passed continually?
